chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Khalil ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ya'qub ibn Yusuf, resident of Isfahan, narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Muqri', known as Abu Dubays, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Ansari narrated from al-Khalil al-Bakri, who said: I heard some of our companions say that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) used to say these excellent words every day of the ten days:

The first of them: 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of nights and eras; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of waves of the seas; 'La ilaha illallah' is better than what they accumulate; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of thorns and trees; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of hair and fur; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of stones and mud; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of the glance of the eyes; 'La ilaha illallah' at night when it darkens and in the morning when it breathes; 'La ilaha illallah' equal to the number of winds in the plains and rocks; 'La ilaha illallah' from this day until the day the Horn is blown.

Al-Khalil said: And I heard him say that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever says that ten times each day of the ten days, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will grant him for each Tahleel a rank in Paradise made of pearls and rubies, and between each two ranks is a journey of one year for a swift rider.

In each rank is a city, in it a castle of a single gem, without partition in it. In each of those cities are pearls, forts, chambers, houses, bedding, spouses, beds, Hoor al-Ayn, cushions, carpets, tables, servants, rivers, trees, jewelry, and garments, which no describer can describe.

So when he emerges from his grave, every hair of his body shines with light, and seventy thousand angels rush to him, walking before him, to his right, and to his left, until he reaches the gate of Paradise.

When he enters it, they stand behind him while he is in front of them, until he reaches a city whose exterior is red ruby and its interior is green emerald, containing all kinds of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created in Paradise.

And when they reach it, they say: 'O beloved of Allah, do you know what this city is and what is in it?' He says: 'No.' They say: 'Who are you?' He says: 'I am the one.' They say: 'We are the angels who witnessed you in the world when you recited Tahleel for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This city and what is in it is a reward for you.'

And rejoice with better than this, the reward of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until you see what Allah has prepared for you in His house, the Abode of Peace, in His proximity, as a gift that never ceases.
Al-Khalil said: So recite it as much as you are able, so that it may increase for you.

key_terms.الصُّور: The Horn (blown on Day of Judgment)
key_terms.الْعَشْرِ: The ten days (specifically of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting La ilaha illallah ten times daily during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the specific devotional practice of Imam Ali (AS) during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, emphasizing the spiritual magnitude of repetitive *Tahlil* (reciting 'La ilaha illallah') with cosmic quantifiers. It underscores the Shia tradition of linking these sacred days with immense eschatological rewards, including unique architectural wonders in Paradise and a celestial reception by seventy thousand angels, reflecting the high status of the Imam's daily liturgy.
